title: Adaptive intake gate for enterprise streamed multi-action requests (chat + tools + structured outputs)
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: We regularly receive complex enterprise requests that combine streaming chat, function/tool calling, and structured output contracts. These requests vary widely in risk, implementation effort, and SLA requirements and currently bounce between PMs, Solutions, and Eng without a consistent outcome. This ticket proposes an adaptive intake gate that classifies incoming enterprise feature requests for hosted API multi-action workflows and routes them to one of: self-serve onboarding, Solutions-assisted pilot, Dedicated capacity eval, or Private deployment presales.

Goal: Define a reproducible triage rubric, automated intake signals, and a playbook for downstream owners so piles of ad-hoc asks are handled predictably and high-risk requests surface early. Outcome should reduce time-to-decision, decrease engineering rework, and make prioritization explicit for stakeholders.

Scope: Non-bug feature requests only. Focus on requests that include any combination of: streaming chat, tool/function calls, and structured outputs (JSON schemas / extractors). Excludes purely embedding/LLM inference requests and infra-only capacity requests (those go to Dedicated).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented triage rubric (scorecard) exists with at least 6 signals and clear thresholds for 4 outcome lanes.
2) Intake form (or enhancements to existing intake) captures required signals (security, data residency, expected QPS, statefulness, success criteria, example prompts/toolchain).
3) Automated classifier prototype (rule-based) implemented in intake pipeline that assigns preliminary lane and confidence.
4) Playbook for each lane (self-serve, Solutions pilot, Dedicated eval, Private) with owners and SLA for response within 3 business days.
5) 3 pilot customer requests processed via the gate and retrospective notes recorded.
6) PM/Eng/Design sign-off on rubric and playbooks.
decisions:
- Use a hybrid scoring model: deterministic rules for security & compliance signals and a weighted numeric score for CPU/token cost, integration complexity, and business priority.
- Initial implementation will be rule-first to avoid model drift and to provide auditability; later iterate with a lightweight ML classifier if volume justifies.
- Default lane mapping: score <= 3 => self-serve; 4-6 => Solutions pilot; 7-9 => Dedicated eval; >=10 or security restrictions => Private.
- Require explicit customer acceptance criteria & success metrics before moving to Solutions pilot.
triage_rubric:
Signals (each 0-3):
- Data sensitivity (0 none, 3 regulated PHI/PCI)
- SLA/latency requirement (0 best-effort, 3 <200ms p95)
- Estimated QPS and burst (0 <10, 3 >200)
- Multi-action complexity (0 single-turn text, 3 multi-tool orchestration with state)
- Structured output strictness (0 free text, 3 rigid JSON schema + schema validation)
- Integration cost (0 client-side only, 3 server side changes + connectors)
Scoring: sum signals; special overrides for legal/compliance flags and customer contract clauses.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (2 weeks): finalise rubric, update intake form, and create playbook drafts.
Phase 1 (3 weeks): implement rule-based classifier in intake (API/webhook), train Solutions and pre-sales on playbooks; process 5 shadow requests.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): run live gate for new enterprise feature requests, collect metrics (time-to-decision, correctness of lane, rework rate).
Phase 3 (iterative): refine thresholds, add optional ML layer, and add UI in Console for intake status.
Rollback: if gate causes >30% increase in request cycle time in first 2 weeks revert to manual triage and iterate offline.

review_feedback: Design: Need example intake UX mockups before Phase 1 (DES-2052 suggested). Ensure minimal friction for self-serve lane.
Security: Recommend including 'KMS/HSM availability' and 'PII handling checklist' as required fields on the intake form.
Eng Reliability: Request to add a 'cost estimate template' to standardize token/QPS estimates and expected autoscaling behavior.
Solutions: Emphasize a customer-facing one-pager per lane to set expectations; include sample SLOs for pilots.
